name: Fifteen Flags and Six Republics: Federations Break Up
description: The end of the Soviet Union and Yugoslavia, and the peaceful split of Czechoslovakia, told through the revolutions, wars and new states of 1989 to 2008.

checkpoints.name: The old federations
checkpoints.note: Soviet rule and Yugoslavia, held together under Tito, bind many nations in single states. In Poland, East Germany and Czechoslovakia, Soviet-backed governments in the Warsaw Pact rule, and Solidarity, led by Lech Walesa, shows the growing unrest of the 1980s.

checkpoints.name: The walls fall
checkpoints.note: The Berlin Wall opens in 1989 and the revolutions of 1989 topple communist governments across Eastern Europe, peacefully in Czechoslovakia's Velvet Revolution and violently in Romania. Germany reunites, and in 1990 Lithuania becomes the first Soviet republic to declare independence under Gorbachev.

checkpoints.name: The republics leave
checkpoints.note: After the failed coup of August 1991 the republics leave one by one, and the Soviet Union is dissolved in December. Slovenia and Croatia declare independence, and war breaks out in the Balkans.

checkpoints.name: Aftermath
checkpoints.note: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully while the Yugoslav wars end in Bosnia and Kosovo. Serbia and Montenegro part in 2006, and Kosovo declares independence in 2008.
